title: Platform systems & services playbook — runbooks, dashboards, alerts, roadmap, and wiki (Q1 2026)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates the Platform Engineering team’s canonical guidance for systems and services owned by the platform: operational runbooks, monitoring and alerting standards, dashboard templates, retrospective cadence and templates, and the near-term roadmap (Q1 2026). The document is intended for oncall engineers, platform owners, SREs, and any downstream service owners who rely on platform primitives (K8s clusters, ingress, auth, storage, GPU fleet gateways).

Scope

- Platform primitives covered: control plane services (platform-api, auth-service), cluster provisioning (kops/eksctl), ingress layer (gateway-api / envoy), CI/CD pipelines (buildkite, tekton tasks), core observability (prometheus, grafana, tempo), and GPU inference gateway (inference-proxy).
- Excluded: customer application logic and model-SDKs. Those teams should rely on this playbook for platform interactions.

Ownership and RACI

- Platform Core (eng-platform): primary owners for runtime, CI/CD, and observability stacks.
- Eng-SRE: incident lead, capacity planning, and SLO ownership enforcement.
- Eng-Serving-Runtime: advisor for inference-proxy and GPU scheduling.
- Product Security: reviews for any changes that increase attack surface.

Service inventory (current)

| Service | Owner | Primary Pager | SLO (p95 latency / availability) | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| platform-api | eng-platform | platform-oncall | 200ms p95 / 99.95% | Public API for platform configuration. Canary deploys required. |
| auth-service | eng-platform | sec-oncall | 100ms p95 / 99.99% | Critical for user flows; separate rate-limits. |
| inference-proxy | eng-serving-runtime | runtime-oncall | 150ms p95 / 99.9% | Routes hosted/dedicated/private inference requests. |
| k8s-control-plane | eng-platform | infra-oncall | N/A / 99.95% | Multi-AZ clusters; automated restore tested monthly. |

SLOs and error budgets

- SLOs are defined per-service in the Service inventory above.
- Error budgets are computed weekly and reported in the SLO dashboard (grafana: /dashboards/slo-overview).
- If a service consumes >50% of error budget in a 7-day window, the owner must open an Action Items epic and schedule a remediation retro within 7 working days.

Dashboards and alerts

Canonical dashboards (Grafana):
1) Platform Overview (cluster health, API latency, total requests, 5xx rate, error budget consumption).
2) GPU Fleet Dashboard (node utilization, GPU memory pressure, preemptible reclaim rate, pod restart rate).
3) CI/CD Health (pipeline success rate, median build time, flaky test ratio).
4) Observability Health (prometheus ingestion lag, scraping failures, long-term storage retention).

Alerting standards (PagerDuty + Slack + Ops channel):
- Alert routing: critical -> pagerduty, page escalation; high -> slack #platform-alerts and email to owners; info -> #platform-notify.
- All alerts must include: brief description, impact, suggested remediation steps, runbook link.

Minimum alert thresholds (examples):
| Alert name | Severity | Trigger | Runbook |
|---|---:|---|---|
| platform-api-5xx-spike | critical | 5xx rate > 1% for 2m and request rate > 100rps | /runbooks/platform-api-5xx.md |
| prometheus-ingest-fallback | high | remote_write failures > 5m | /runbooks/prometheus-remote-write.md |
| gpu-memory-pressure | critical | GPU memory alloc > 90% on >20% nodes | /runbooks/gpu-pressure.md |

Runbooks and how-tos

Runbook: platform-api 5xx spike (summary)
1) Triage: Check Grafana Platform Overview and logs in Loki for 5xx patterns.
2) Scope: Run a query: "sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"platform-api\",status=~\"5..\"}[2m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"platform-api\"}[2m]))" to validate.
3) Temporary mitigation: Increase replica count by +2 (kubectl scale deployment/platform-api --replicas=$(current+2)) and enable circuit-breaker fallback for non-critical routes.
4) Rollback/Deploy: If a recent deploy is suspected, open the release dashboard and initiate rollback to previous stable revision.
5) Post-incident: Tag incident, record root cause, estimate customer impact, and schedule a remediation epic if needed.

How-to: Add a new alert (step-by-step)
1) Propose alert in the #platform-alerts channel with motivation and intended runbook.
2) Create alert rule in prometheus/rules/platform.rules.yml with a sensible duration (e.g., 2m for critical).
3) Add Grafana panel and link to runbook.
4) Submit PR to infra repo, include test queries and simulated firing details.
5) After merge, notify oncall and monitor for 48 hours. If alert is noisy, iterate and tune thresholds.

Example alert rule (yaml snippet)

- alert: platform_api_5xx_spike
  expr: |
    sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"platform-api\",status=~\"5..\"}[2m]))
    / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"platform-api\"}[2m])) > 0.01
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    summary: "platform-api 5xx rate > 1%"
    runbook: "/runbooks/platform-api-5xx.md"

Incident triage template

1) Detect and acknowledge (0–5m): Acknowledge pager duty, set incident channel (#inc-<id>).
2) Triage (5–15m): Determine blast radius, affected customers, and whether rollback is required.
3) Mitigation (15–60m): Apply quick mitigations (scale, rate-limit, feature-flag).
4) RCA and recovery (60m+): Restore full service and collect diagnostics.
5) Postmortem (72 hours): Publish a postmortem including timeline, root cause, and action items.

Retrospective cadence and template

- Frequency: Platform team retros every sprint (2 weeks). Incident retros active after any Sev2+ or service >50% error budget.
- Template: Summary, timeline, what went well, what went poorly, action items, owners, target dates.

Roadmap (Q1 2026 priorities)

- Observability hardening (Feb 2026): Implement long-term metrics retention and prometheus remote_read failover; target: reduce data-loss events to <1/month.
- GPU autoscaler beta (Mar 2026): Launch horizontal GPU autoscaler for inference jobs to reduce cost by 15% on average.
- Alert taxonomy and playbook rollout (Mar 2026): Standardize alert severities and train oncall with tabletop exercises.
- Platform self-service UX (Apr 2026): New console pages to onboard namespaces and grant least-privilege roles with one-click templates.

Operational tooling and runbooks repository

- Primary repo: git@github.com:redwood/platform-infra (rules, dashboards, runbooks in /runbooks).
- Docs: confluence:eng-platform team wiki organizes how-tos and links to runbooks.
- Oncall rotas and escalation policies are maintained in PagerDuty and mirrored in the team wiki.

Oncall responsibilities and playbook enforcement

- Oncall engineers must: keep runbooks updated after incidents, own scheduled runbook drills per quarter, and confirm dashboard alerts are actionable.
- Owners must tag any new service with an SLO and add it to the SLO dashboard before rolling to production.

Appendix: useful commands and queries

- Check cluster node status: kubectl get nodes -o wide
- Scale deployment: kubectl scale deployment/<name> --replicas=3 -n platform
- Query 5xx ratio: (PromQL snippet already shown above)
- Tail logs (loki): loki query: {job=\"platform-api\"} | logfmt | line_format

Related pages and links

- Platform runbooks index: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks-index
- SLO dashboard: grafana/redwood/slo-overview
- Oncall guide: /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-guide-2025
